review_notice: These are source-grounded candidate viewpoints extracted from published papers. They are not independent replications or endorsements by the original authors.

papers.title: On the Distribution of Firing Rates in Networks of Cortical Neurons
papers.claim: In the analysed fluctuation-driven network models, an expansive single-neuron input-output nonlinearity can transform approximately symmetric input distributions into long-tailed firing-rate distributions.
papers.evidence: Analytical and numerical analyses of leaky integrate-and-fire and conductance-based network models.
papers.scope: Randomly connected cortical network models in the parameter regimes analysed in the paper.
papers.non_claim: This does not establish that the same mechanism uniquely explains every empirical cortical firing-rate distribution.

papers.title: Voltage- and Branch-Specific Climbing Fiber Responses in Purkinje Cells
papers.claim: In the analysed Purkinje-cell models, climbing-fibre responses and their energetic cost depend on dendritic voltage and branch identity.
papers.evidence: Compartmental modelling of climbing-fibre input, potassium-current availability, calcium influx and energy consumption.
papers.scope: Purkinje-cell dendritic responses under the model and stimulation conditions studied.
papers.non_claim: Somatic complex-spike duration alone is not treated as a complete readout of dendritic climbing-fibre bursting.

papers.title: Targeted Activation of Hippocampal Place Cells Drives Memory-Guided Spatial Behavior
papers.claim: Targeted activation of small hippocampal place-cell ensembles biased mice toward the spatial behaviour associated with those cells.
papers.evidence: All-optical two-photon imaging and targeted optogenetic stimulation during virtual-reality navigation.
papers.scope: The place-cell ensembles, behavioural task and mouse preparation tested in the study.
papers.non_claim: The result does not imply that place cells alone are sufficient for all forms of spatial memory.

papers.title: The Neuronal Perturbome in Mouse Visual Cortex
papers.claim: Single-cell perturbations in mouse visual cortex produce heterogeneous local influence patterns that cannot be inferred from activity correlations alone.
papers.evidence: Targeted neuronal perturbation combined with population recording in visual cortex.
papers.scope: Local cortical effects measured in the experimental preparation and visual conditions used by the study.
papers.non_claim: The measured perturbation map is not a complete anatomical connectome or a universal causal circuit model.

papers.title: Metabolically Regulated Spiking Could Serve Neuronal Energy Homeostasis and Protect from Reactive Oxygen Species
papers.claim: The proposed models show that self-initiated spiking can act as an energy-release mechanism that stabilizes mitochondrial metabolic variables and limits reactive oxygen species under low demand.
papers.evidence: Models coupling ATP, ADP and reactive oxygen species to firing, including a ROS-modulated ion-channel model and cortical avalanche simulations.
papers.scope: A computational existence result under the metabolic assumptions and parameter regimes analysed.
papers.non_claim: The paper does not demonstrate in vivo that metabolic homeostasis is the unique cause of spontaneous neuronal activity.

papers.title: A Drosophila Computational Brain Model Reveals Sensorimotor Processing
papers.claim: A whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model built from Drosophila connectivity and neurotransmitter identity generated experimentally testable predictions for feeding and grooming circuits.
papers.evidence: Connectome-constrained simulation followed by optogenetic and behavioural validation of selected predictions.
papers.scope: Adult Drosophila sensorimotor circuits and the model assumptions tested in the paper.
papers.non_claim: Connectivity and transmitter identity are not claimed to explain every neural computation or behavioural context.

papers.title: Emergence and Effective Information in Data-Driven Dynamical Systems
papers.claim: Maximizing effective information can learn coarse-grained latent dynamics with stronger estimated causal effects and improved out-of-environment generalization in the tested systems.
papers.evidence: Machine-learning framework evaluated on simulated systems, real data and an fMRI coarse-graining example.
papers.scope: The causal-emergence objective, models and datasets analysed by the study.
papers.non_claim: A learned macro-state is not automatically a uniquely correct ontology of the underlying system.

papers.title: High Capacity and Dynamic Accessibility in Associative Memory Networks with Context-Dependent Neuronal and Synaptic Gating
papers.claim: In context-modular associative-memory networks, neuronal or synaptic gating can reduce cross-context interference and trade memory accessibility against storage capacity.
papers.evidence: Analytical and numerical study of random gating and context-specific synaptic refinement.
papers.scope: The associative-memory model classes and gating protocols introduced in the paper.
papers.non_claim: The framework is not direct evidence that biological memory uses the same gating implementation.

papers.title: A General Framework for Interpretable Neural Learning Based on Local Information-Theoretic Goal Functions
papers.claim: Parameterized local goals derived from partial information decomposition can train infomorphic networks on supervised, unsupervised and memory tasks while retaining an interpretable local objective.
papers.evidence: Derivation of a local learning rule and computational demonstrations across several learning paradigms.
papers.scope: The neuron model, PID parameterization, architectures and tasks evaluated in the paper.
papers.non_claim: Task performance does not by itself establish that the learning rule is biologically implemented.

papers.title: Linking Functional Activity and Connectivity of Neuronal Circuits via Fast Cross-Layer All-Optical Physiology
papers.claim: The CLAOP system can combine fast cross-layer two-photon recording with targeted optogenetic manipulation to map functional activity-connectivity relations across cortical layers.
papers.evidence: Instrument validation and all-optical measurements in visual, somatosensory and hippocampal circuits.
papers.scope: The optical preparation, spatial-temporal resolution and circuit examples tested.
papers.non_claim: Functional influence measured by the system is not identical to a complete anatomical connectivity map.

papers.title: A Brain-Wide Map of Neural Activity during Complex Behaviour
papers.claim: Across a standardized decision task, sensory, choice, movement and prior-related signals were distributed across many brain regions with distinct spatial and temporal profiles.
papers.evidence: 621,733 neurons recorded with 699 Neuropixels probes across 139 mice and 12 laboratories.
papers.scope: The standardized mouse decision-making task, recorded areas and analyses reported by the International Brain Laboratory.
papers.non_claim: Widespread encoding does not establish that every recorded region is causally necessary for each variable.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Computing Paradigms Enhance Robustness through Spiking Neural Networks
papers.claim: In the evaluated CIFAR-10 adversarial setting, temporal encoding, early-exit decoding and specialized training improved spiking-network robustness relative to the matched artificial-network baselines.
papers.evidence: Adversarial robustness experiments and ablations on temporal processing and encoding strategies.
papers.scope: The datasets, attacks, architectures, training methods and energy estimates used in the study.
papers.non_claim: The reported advantage is not a universal robustness guarantee for all spiking networks or attacks.

papers.title: Deconstructing Dynamics of Symmetry Breaking
papers.claim: Analytical solutions of order-parameter dynamics in the studied Landau-Ginzburg settings explain why the temporal freeze-out construction reproduces Kibble-Zurek scaling.
papers.evidence: Analytical treatment of temporal and spatial order-parameter evolution with proposed experimentally accessible observables.
papers.scope: The phase-transition models and approximations analysed in the paper.
papers.non_claim: The derivation does not make every real symmetry-breaking system equivalent to the analysed models.

papers.title: Artificial Neural Manifolds
papers.claim: A Mott-memristor architecture can construct a low-dimensional artificial neural manifold for small-sample prediction, with a memory factor improving robustness in the tested tasks.
papers.evidence: Device circuits, delay-embedding formulation and demonstrations on incomplete-image perception and seizure prediction.
papers.scope: The hardware architecture, spatiotemporal information equation and benchmark tasks reported.
papers.non_claim: Similarity to biological tuning curves does not establish biological equivalence.

papers.title: Human Cortical Networks Trade Communication Efficiency for Computational Reliability
papers.claim: In the study's generative and reservoir-computing analyses, human cortical topology sacrifices wiring and communication efficiency for greater robustness of computation to targeted disruption.
papers.evidence: Game-theoretic network growth, reservoir-computing comparison and virtual lesion analyses.
papers.scope: Human structural-network data and the propagation, optimization and lesion models used.
papers.non_claim: The result does not imply that communication efficiency is irrelevant or that the model uniquely explains cortical topology.

papers.title: A Language Network in the Individualized Functional Connectomes of 1199 Human Brains Doing Arbitrary Tasks
papers.claim: Individualized functional connectomes from arbitrary-task fMRI recovered a predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal network that was stable within people and selective for language.
papers.evidence: 1,957 fMRI sessions from 1,199 people analysed with individualized functional connectomics.
papers.scope: The datasets, preprocessing, parcellations and language-localization tests reported.
papers.non_claim: Functional-connectivity recovery does not uniquely specify the causal computations of language.

papers.title: Preconfigured Neuronal Firing Sequences in Human Brain Organoids
papers.claim: Structured spontaneous firing sequences appeared in human and mouse brain organoids and neonatal mouse cortical slices, but not in dissociated primary cortical cultures.
papers.evidence: Cross-preparation recordings and sequence analyses in organoids, ex vivo cortex and dissociated cultures.
papers.scope: The developmental stages, preparations and sequence metrics tested.
papers.non_claim: The observations do not show that all mature sequence structure is independent of experience.

papers.title: Simple Input-Output Dependencies Explain Neuronal Activity
papers.claim: Across the neuronal datasets studied, models containing direct input-output dependencies without explicit input interactions explained most measured activity variability and predicted higher-order dependencies.
papers.evidence: Quantitative model comparison across multiple brain regions and species, with inferred connectivity analyses.
papers.scope: The binary activity representations, datasets and dependency models analysed.
papers.non_claim: Good predictive performance does not establish that biophysical input interactions are absent.

papers.title: Predictability of Complex Networks
papers.claim: Mapping link prediction to a spin-glass model yields a predictability index and decomposes global link predictability into local contributions in the analysed network ensembles.
papers.evidence: Cavity-method derivations, exact results for canonical models and analyses of real networks.
papers.scope: The link-prediction formulation, random division protocol and network models considered.
papers.non_claim: The predictability index is not a guarantee that every practical algorithm reaches the bound.

papers.title: Population Geometry Reveals Shared Latent Structure
papers.claim: The study links specific population-geometry statistics to task-efficient representation of shared latent structure across the tested settings.
papers.evidence: Population-geometry analyses and computational comparisons reported in the paper.
papers.scope: The neural datasets, latent variables and target computations evaluated.
papers.non_claim: Geometric similarity does not by itself establish a unique neural mechanism.

papers.title: Emotional-State Geometry in the Basolateral Amygdala
papers.claim: Basolateral-amygdala population activity in the tested threat paradigm contained a geometry that supported specialized readout of emotional state across behavioural conditions.
papers.evidence: Population recordings, behavioural measurements, decoding and perturbation analyses in mice.
papers.scope: The virtual-burrow assay, aversive conditions and recorded basolateral-amygdala populations.
papers.non_claim: The geometry is not asserted to be a complete or universal representation of emotion.

papers.title: Machine, Organism and Language: An Epistemology of AI Models
papers.claim: The essay argues that contemporary AI is best understood through the historical recombination of machine, organism and language paradigms, and as an automation of relational structures embedded in social cooperation.
papers.evidence: Comparative historical and philosophical analysis drawing on epistemology, political economy and histories of computation.
papers.scope: A conceptual argument rather than an empirical or causal neuroscience claim.
papers.non_claim: The essay does not experimentally test a computational mechanism or biological model.
